title: Automated Robotic Liquid Handling Assembly of Modular DNA Devices
protocol: Navigate to mocloassembly.com using a web browser.
Upload Genbank files for all DNA parts that will be included in the combinatorial DNA device design.
Select desired DNA parts and drag them onto the blank canvas, placing part types in the intended final order of DNA parts.
Click 'Assemble' on the bottom right of the page.
Navigate to the 'Plans' tab and download files generated by the tool.
These files will include human-readable plate maps for preparing DNA samples and reagents necessary for reactions.
Download a picklist for the liquid handler from the generated files.
Download fully annotated Genbank files for all DNA devices to be assembled.
Streak out bacterial glycerol stocks onto LB-agar plates supplemented with the appropriate antibiotic.
Incubate plates at 37°C overnight.
Inoculate 3 mL of LB broth (supplemented with appropriate antibiotic) with a single colony from the LB-agar plates.
Incubate cultures overnight at 37°C while shaking at 300 RPM.
Purify plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures using a mini-prep plasmid purification kit.
Dilute each sample of plasmid DNA to a concentration of 20 fmol/μL in water or TE buffer.
Place the indicated volume of each diluted DNA part into the appropriate well on a full-skirted 96-well PCR plate according to the MoClo_Setup.xlsx file and PDF assembly tool.
Hold the SetupPlate on ice until needed, or seal with a foil adhesive seal and store at -20°C.
Mix 2 μL of 10x T4 DNA ligase buffer with each 20 µL of reaction on ice.
Add 0.5 µL of T4 DNA Ligase (HC) to each reaction mixture on ice.
Pipette 1 µL of BsaI enzyme into each reaction mixture on ice.
Distribute the enzyme mastermix into appropriate wells of a new full-skirted 96-well PCR plate following the plate map for the ReagentPlate.
Place the SetupPlate(s) and ReagentPlate(s) (on a 96-well cold-block) on the deck of the liquid handler.
Prepare empty full-skirted 96-well PCR plates as OutputPlates and place them on the deck of the liquid handler.
Create instances of each sample and reagent plate in the control software, naming them exactly as they appear on the generated plate maps.
Name a trough of clean, deionized water 'Reservoir' in the control software.
Load the .gwl file generated by mocloassembly.com using the ‘Worklist’ command in the control software.
Execute another ‘Worklist’ command to run the .gwl file loaded previously.
Use the controller software's 'Run' command to execute the script.
Allow the robotic liquid handler to complete script execution before accessing deck space.
Remove all plates from the liquid handler deck after use.
Seal SetupPlate(s) with aluminum sealing film and store at -20°C if saving remaining DNA.
Seal OutputPlate(s) with adhesive film upon completion of reactions.
Place sealed OutputPlate(s) in a thermocycler or heat block.
Run thermocycling with parameters: 37 °C for 2 h, 50 °C for 5 min, 80 °C for 10 min, hold at 4 °C.
Thaw competent E. coli cell aliquots (10 µL/reaction) on ice before transformation.
Prepare LB-agar plates with appropriate antibiotic as required.
Pipette 50 μL of 0.1 M IPTG and 50 μL of 20 mg/mL X-GAL onto plate surface for each reaction or prepare a master mix if plating many reactions.
Coat plates evenly using sterile glass rod or beads.
Allow coated plates to rest at 37 °C for at least 15 min before use.
Aliquot 10 µL of competent cells into each well of a new 96-well PCR plate.
Add 1-3 µL of each reaction from the OutputPlate(s) to the corresponding wells in the Transformation Plate.
Incubate the Transformation Plate on ice for 5 min.
Seal the Transformation Plate with adhesive film.
Heat shock the Transformation Plate at 42 °C for 30 s in a thermocycler.
Place the plate on ice immediately after heat shock for 2 min.
Add 150 µL of SOC media to each well of the Transformation Plate.
Seal the Transformation Plate with an aluminum adhesive seal.
Incubate the Transformation Plate at 37 °C while shaking at 900 RPM for 1 hr.
Plate the full contents of each well from the Transformation Plate onto LB-agar plates using a sterile glass rod or glass beads to evenly coat the surface of the plate.
Incubate the LB-agar plates at 37 °C overnight.
Prepare one or several 96-well deep-well culture blocks with 1.5 mL of LB broth containing appropriate antibiotic.
Inoculate the deep-well culture block(s) with single white colonies from each LB-agar plate of transformed reactions.
Seal the culture block(s) with a gas-permeable seal.
Incubate the culture block(s) overnight at 37 °C while shaking at 900 RPM.
Isolate plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures.
Submit isolated plasmid DNA for Sanger sequencing to verify clones.
